brief_rationale: The trajectory met the postoperative responsibility chain: the doctor kept the episode focused on right-eye cataract aftercare, screened and escalated red flags, clarified drops and later additions, built a rotating-caregiver paper/group-chat execution system, arranged ophthalmology follow-up, and kept diabetes/hypertension management bounded. There were no serious or minor responsibility-chain errors visible; residual uncertainties were assigned to discharge papers/ophthalmology or routine monitoring rather than left blocking. HO1, HO3, and HO4 were actively completed with meaningful impact, while HO2 was only partially completed because the left-versus-right history was recognized but not deeply reconstructed beyond the minimum. This supports a Perfect grade under the case rule requiring no chain error and at least two completed high-order points.
